topic: Ideation, User Journey Mapping, and Solution Exploration
learningObjectives: Generate multiple solution ideas from a defined user problem.
Map user emotions, actions, and pain points across a journey.
Select concepts for further exploration using clear criteria.

activities.title: User Journey Map
activities.instruction: Explore the user's actions, emotions, pain points, and opportunities across a complete journey.

content.concept: A journey map visualizes user stages, actions, thoughts, emotions, pain points, and opportunities across an experience.
content.tip: Select each journey stage to reveal what the user is doing, thinking, and feeling.

items.label: Discover
items.description: The user becomes aware of the product or service.

items.label: Explore
items.description: The user compares available options and gathers information.

items.label: Decide
items.description: The user evaluates options and chooses an action.

items.label: Complete
items.description: The user performs the main task or transaction.

items.label: Post-Task
items.description: The user receives confirmation, support, or follow-up information.

activities.title: Journey Sequencer
activities.instruction: Arrange the user's actions in the correct order.

content.concept: Mapping actions in sequence helps reveal friction points and opportunities throughout the complete user experience.
content.tip: Think about what the user needs to do before each subsequent action becomes possible.

activities.title: Ideation Builder
activities.instruction: Arrange solution ideas from broad possibilities toward concepts ready for further exploration.

content.concept: Ideation expands the solution space by generating multiple possibilities before narrowing toward promising concepts.
content.tip: Separate idea generation from evaluation so that the team explores multiple possibilities before choosing.

activities.title: Concept Selection Lab
activities.instruction: Select the concept that best satisfies the given user and product criteria.

content.concept: Early concepts can be compared using factors such as user value, feasibility, clarity, and alignment with the problem.
content.tip: Consider multiple criteria rather than selecting an idea simply because it looks interesting.

scenarios.question: The team needs a solution that provides high user value and can be prototyped quickly.
options: A feature unrelated to the user's problem
scenarios.explanation: The concept directly addresses the problem while remaining practical to prototype.

scenarios.question: A concept is technically impressive but does not address the identified user need.
scenarios.explanation: Concept selection should remain connected to the validated problem.

separation.learning: Teach the concept through an interactive experience.
separation.assessment: Stored separately and completed after learning.
separation.practical: Stored separately and completed after assessment.
